newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE Brent set lower but brake seen on fall.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE Brent set lower but brake seen on fall.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* Slow momentum continues to point the market lower though good support levels are in place to brake rapid falls. * Upside on the spot month chart appears limited to Wednesday's high of $18.32 with initial support to the down side at around $17.60 and then $17.32 last week's 13-month low.
IPE Brent crude futures are set to continue to move lower, but slowly, with several good support levels in place to brake any rapid falls, analysts said.

They said a bearish gap down on the Brent front month continuation chart between $18.02, the low on Tuesday and $17.98, the high of Wednesday was neutralised by a similar gap-up between $17.98 and $18.02 from Monday to Tuesday.
"I wouldn't exactly call it an island reversal of the recent small uptrend, but market momentum looks likely to continue towards the down side," Darren Gurner at Sucden said.
"The market has support but in the long term will be heading down to new lows," Gurner added.
Analysts said the upside on the spot month chart appears limited to Wednesday's high of $18.32 with initial support around $17.60 and then $17.32 last week's 13-month low.

Looking at the second month continuation chart Gurner said: "We are well below the 50 percent Fibonacci retracement level and could quite easily be looking at the 100 percent retracement marker at $16.58 soon".
August Brent crude futures on SIMEX were quoted at $17.70/$17.85 after London fell 31 cents to $17.77 per barrel on Wednesday.
NYMEX July, which expires on Friday, was last traded on ACCESS at $18.79 per barrel unchanged from the close, while August was last traded at $18.97, up one cent.
Spot WTI broke a trendline on Wednesday extending from the 16-month low of $18.41 it made June 11, some brokers felt July crude could test that level again before the contract expires Friday.
Spot gasoline is seen testing support at 56.00 cents, an area carved out and tested last week on three consecutive sessions. --Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
